faq.q1: How do I assign tasks to a group?
faq.a1: Create a group on Wie-Doet-Het, add your tasks and share the link via WhatsApp. Participants click on the task they want to do. You can instantly see who picked what.
faq.a2: Wie-Doet-Het is a free app that lets you easily divide tasks among a group. Ideal for sports, school, parties and volunteering. Participants don't need an account.
faq.a3: Yes, Wie-Doet-Het is completely free to use. Create an account as an organiser and invite participants via a share link — they don't need to sign up anywhere.
faq.q4: Can I divide tasks via WhatsApp?
faq.a4: After creating a task list you generate a share link that you paste directly into your WhatsApp group. Participants open the link and claim their task without an extra app or account.

about.title: About Wie-Doet-Het
about.intro: Wie-Doet-Het is a free web app for assigning tasks across a group of people, without everyone needing an account.

sections.title: The problem
paragraphs: Tasks usually get assigned in a WhatsApp group. Someone pastes a list, twenty messages later nobody has an overview: two people take the same task, three tasks are left undone, and the organiser has to keep track by hand. Existing project tools solve that with accounts, invitations and permissions — far too heavy for "who is bringing the deposit bottles".

sections.title: How Wie-Doet-Het solves it
paragraphs: The organiser creates a group, adds the tasks and shares one link. Everyone who opens the link sees the complete list and picks what they will do. A claimed task is immediately visible to everyone, so duplicated work cannot happen. Per task you can set how many people may sign up.
Participants do not create an account. They only enter their name on the task they take. Only the organiser needs an account, to find the group again later and change it.

sections.title: What it is used for
paragraphs: Sports clubs dividing canteen shifts, class parents organising a school party, housemates getting the cleaning rota sorted, volunteers keeping an event running, and families dividing Christmas between the cook, the groceries and the washing-up.

sections.title: What it is not
paragraphs: Not a project management tool, not a chat, not a calendar and not time tracking. Wie-Doet-Het does one thing: a list of tasks, a shared link, and making visible who takes what.

sections.title: About the project
paragraphs: Wie-Doet-Het is an independent, free project. The source code of the web app is public on GitHub.

link.label: View the source code on GitHub

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: Wie-Doet-Het is a small, free project. Below you will find where to go for each situation, so you do not knock on the wrong door.

sections.title: You have been invited to a task list
paragraphs: Questions about a specific group — which task you get, when something is due, whether you may swap — do not go through us. The person who sent you the share link is the organiser of that group and manages the list. Contact them directly, in the group chat where you received the link.

sections.title: You found a bug or miss a feature
paragraphs: Report it as an issue on the public repository. Include which browser you use, what you did and what you expected. If it concerns a specific group: do not share a share link in a public issue — that link gives anyone access to the task list.

sections.title: You want your account or data deleted
paragraphs: Delete your groups in the app and then your account via your profile page. What is still kept afterwards, and for how long, is described on the privacy page.

sections.title: You are an AI agent
paragraphs: Start with the agent guide for what the product does and when you should or should not recommend it. Wie-Doet-Het is a website that people use in a browser; there is nothing for an agent to log in to.

sections.title: What there is not
paragraphs: There is no phone number, no support desk and no guaranteed response time. This is not a company with a customer service department — it is a free tool maintained by a single maintainer. Reports on GitHub are read, but a reply may take a while.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Wie-Doet-Het collects as little as possible. This page describes exactly which data exists, why it exists and how you get rid of it.

sections.title: As an organiser (with an account)
paragraphs: To create a group you need an account. For that we store:
items: your name, as you enter it yourself;
your email address, as a login name and to find your account again;
your password, stored encrypted — not readable by us;
the groups and tasks you create.
sections.after: Your email address is not sold, not shared with advertisers and not used for newsletters.

sections.title: As a participant (without an account)
paragraphs: Participants do not have to sign up for anything. Someone who claims a task via a share link only leaves behind:
items: the name they type in themselves on that task;
a random session ID in the browser, so you can find and withdraw your own claim on the same device;
sections.after: No email address, phone number or profile of participants is stored.

sections.title: The share link
paragraphs: A group's share link works as a key: anyone who has the link can view the task list and claim a task. So only share it with the people who belong in that group, and do not put it on a public page.

sections.title: Storage in your browser
paragraphs: After logging in, a session token is placed in your browser's local storage so you stay logged in. Logging out or clearing your browser data removes the token. Participants without an account only have the session ID above.

sections.title: Statistics
paragraphs: The site uses Google Analytics 4 to count which pages are visited. That concerns page views, not the content of your tasks or the names of participants. If you do not want this, block analytics scripts in your browser or with an extension — the app keeps working.

sections.title: Deleting
paragraphs: If you delete a group, the tasks and claims of that group disappear with it. If you delete your account, your account data and the groups you manage disappear.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: If anything about what we store changes, this page is updated and the date in the sitemap is refreshed.

useWhen: The user wants to divide concrete chores across several people.
The group is reachable through a group chat rather than a shared project tool.
Examples: household chores, who brings what to a party, volunteer shifts, moving-day jobs.
avoidWhen: Project plans with dependencies and deadlines.
Situations where a manager has to assign the work from above.
care: A claim is visible to the whole group; never suggest claiming on behalf of a third party.
The share link is the secret: treat it like a password and do not repeat it in a shared or logged environment.
A task can have a maximum number of participants; do not promise a spot without checking the group view.
Do not create groups, claim tasks or log in on behalf of the user.
